item.title: Some small businesses in Juneau speak out against ICE amid nationwide strike
item.description: Several downtown storefronts closed for the day while others took a stance in other ways.

item.title: Juneau School Board seeks feedback for superintendent search
item.description: The Juneau School District Board of Education is working with a search firm to collect feedback from the community before it makes a hiring decision.

item.title: Alaska House passes bill tightening residency requirements for hunting and fishing licenses
item.description: The bipartisan bill aims to close a loophole that allows some Alaskans to hunt and fish as residents despite spending little time in the state.

item.title: Yes, it’s another government shutdown, but Alaska impacts might be minimal
item.description: Both Alaska U.S. senators helped pass a bill to fund much of the government. Now it's the House's turn. The funding lapse could last as little as one weekday.

item.title: Trump administration denies full disaster funding for Western Alaska storms, state files appeal
item.description: Alaska’s Republican congressional delegation said they support the state’s appeal, and are urging FEMA and the Trump administration to fund the disaster relief effort.

item.title: Juneau’s emergency manager talks planning, response and recovery in wake of local disaster
item.description: Emergency Programs Manager Ryan O’Shaughnessy shares lessons learned from the major storm events in December and January and how the department operates.

item.title: Forest Service moves forward with logging project near Ketchikan
item.description: Most of the harvest will be old-growth trees, which some people worry will be devastating to the forest.

item.title: North Douglas boat launch to reopen later this week following sinkhole closure
item.description: Juneau’s Docks and Harbors staff closed off a portion of the launch’s parking lot in mid-January after discovering a large sinkhole near the entrance.

item.title: Coast Guard’s new Juneau base may not be complete until 2029, commandant says
item.description: Adm. Lunday, top officer of Coast Guard, says he is considering whether to base four new icebreakers in Alaska.

item.title: Newscast – Monday, Feb. 2, 2026
